In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chiral-invariance factorization scheme is more consistent with the QCD factorization theorems, while the AB-like scheme is less consistent.
the next-to-leading order QCD analysis of the polarized structure function data in the AB scheme is inconsistent with QCD.

, in order for the QCD analysis in next-to-leading-order to be consistent with perturbative QED, the axial anomaly should reside in the gluon contribution to the first moment, and the quark distribution should be free of the axial anomaly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the next-to-leading order polarized QCD analysis should be performed, instead of the AB scheme, in the factorization scheme which is consistent with chiral symmetry, i.e., the scheme in which the anomaly resides in the hard gluon coefficient function.
the chiral-invariance is a fundamental property of QCD, and it should be maintained in all physical observables, especially the first moments of structure functions. [1]

, in the chiro-invariant scheme, the next-to-leading order correction is small and the data can be described with a reasonable value of Λ 2, and the factorization scheme dependence of the first moment of the polarized structure function g 1 (x) is not large.
The main takeaway from our work is that
one can not simply use a different factorization scheme to fit the same data and then compare with a different scheme, as is often done, without considering the effect of the axial anomaly.
the AB scheme should be avoided in QCD analysis of inclusive polarized structure functions. [1]
the chiral-invariance factorization scheme is more consistent with QCD and should be used for the next-to-leading order QCD analysis of g 1.
